column11: JUDGEMENT: the first-line line (HARMONi-3 NCT05899608 and HARMONi-7 NCT06767514, Phase 3) is now the whole asset, so pos is that line's own probability, no longer a blend. It is set between two published rates. Upper, 0.439: oncology Phase 3 to approval, BIO/Informa/QLS Clinical Development Success Rates 2011-2020, Figure 2, 47.7% x 92.0% (data/pos_by_area.csv), which counts a Phase 3 as a success on any primary endpoint, PFS included. Lower, 0.257: Sherry AD et al., JAMA Oncol 2025;11(7):718-724, doi:10.1001/jamaoncol.2025.1002, PMID 40451185: of 791 superiority Phase 3 oncology trials published 2002 to 2024, 53% (420) met their primary endpoint but 28% (221) showed OS superiority, so 221/791 x 92.0% = 0.257. The midpoint, (0.257 + 0.439) / 2 = 0.348, is a judgement, not a measurement
column12: why the bar moved: the complete response letter of 2026-11-15 says PFS without significant OS 'does not support a positive benefit-risk profile' for ivonescimab (8-K 0001599298-26-000092), in a setting where Summit says no approved regimen had shown OS. First line is a harder setting for that test, since the comparator, pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, has proven OS, so a first-line approval on PFS alone is not a case this book should price; HARMONi-3's OS is a primary endpoint in each cohort and Summit sized both cohorts 'to sufficiently power for both primary endpoints (PFS and OS)' (Q3 2026 10-Q, 0001599298-26-000090; FY2025 10-K, 0001599298-26-000015). The case for higher: those trials are powered for OS, which many of Sherry's 791 were not; ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab on OS in HARMONi-2, HR 0.73, p=0.009 (8-K 0001599298-26-000078), and there are three shots (two HARMONi-3 cohorts and HARMONi-7). The case for lower: HARMONi-2 and HARMONi-A ran in China, and the global HARMONi, with 165 of 438 patients western (8-K 0001599298-26-000081), missed OS. Before the letter this row was 0.403661, a blend with the post-TKI line at 0.1212; stepping to the seed's own failure leg on 0.439 gives rNPV $1,655.8mm against $1,312.5mm at 0.348

column11: published, for the event the engine prices these legs on, HARMONi-3's squamous primary PFS analysis (NCT05899608, Q4 2026; the earliest catalyst citing the study). A PFS win is not an approval: the FDA refused HARMONi on PFS without significant OS on 2026-11-15 (8-K 0001599298-26-000092). So the leg is the chance a trial that meets its primary endpoint also shows OS superiority, times filing to approval. Sherry et al., JAMA Oncol 2025, PMID 40451185: of 791 Phase 3 oncology trials 53% (about 419) met their primary endpoint and 221 showed OS superiority, 221/419 = 0.527, taking the OS winners as a subset of those that met it. Times oncology NDA/BLA to approval 0.920 (BIO/Informa/QLS 2011-2020, Figure 2, data/pos_by_area.csv): 0.485
